newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Currency woes wane but C&C drains Singapore stocks.
newsitem.headline: Currency woes wane but C&C drains Singapore stocks.

text.p: The Singapore stock market seemed to get over regional currency woes on Wednesday morning but was promptly hit by poor sentiment in blue chip car retailer Cycle and Carriage, dealers said.
"Currency worries have quietened. It's basically one counter play this morning. Cycle & Carriage was responsible for the fall," a local dealer said.
By 0430 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index had shed 18.32 to 1,918.77, led by C&C.

The car and property firm fell to a new low of Singapore $12.50 on 333,000 shares traded. Dealers said poor sentiment on the property market and the rising price of putting a car on the road were weighing on the stock.
"Cycle & Carriage has been falling since it broke the S$14 support. It could now look to test S$11-12," said a dealer.
Breadmaker QAF led the actives with over 3.4 million shares trade after major shareholder Salim said it would inject giant noodle maker Indofood into the company.
QAF shares were down six cents to S$1.74 on concerns over the huge financing needed for the acquisition.
Raffles Medical rose nine cents to S$1.31 with over 2.9 million shares on renewed takeover and merger speculation.
Multimedia Creative Technolgy rose to a high of S$32 before easing to S$31.90 reflecting gains in U.S. high tech stocks.
Total market volume was light at around 70 million shares with 128 gainers to 170 losers.
